title: One bag, four frames
scenario:
A coffee roaster launches a new bag of beans. You need one product image in four placements: a square post, a website header, a very wide email banner and a tall phone story.

Your draft plan is to make one square image and crop it four ways. The exhibit shows the brief, your plan and the size rules you copied from the docs.
exhibit:
Brief
  Client: Northfield Roasters. One new coffee bag, four placements.
  1  Square social post (1:1)
  2  Website header (16:9)
  3  Email banner (4:1, very wide)
  4  Phone story (9:16, tall)
  Every image: the bag sharp, the beans in close detail.

Your draft plan
  - Generate one 1024x1024 square on an OpenAI GPT Image model.
  - Crop that square to make the other three placements.
  - Prompt: "A coffee bag, nice angle, beautiful lens, good framing."

Size rules from the docs (shortened)
  OpenAI custom size: both edges multiples of 16, no edge over
    3,840 px, long edge no more than 3x the short edge.
  Gemini, Nano Banana 2.1: aspect_ratio list includes
    1:1, 4:1, 9:16 and 16:9.

questions.prompt: Which prompt gives the camera the clearest direction for this brief?

options.text: "A coffee bag, the nicest angle, the most beautiful lens, the best framing, perfect composition."
options.explanation: These words praise the camera but don't say where it is or which lens to use.

options.text: "A coffee bag on an oak counter, close-up at eye level, macro lens, 100mm, sharp focus on the beans."
options.explanation: Right. It names the distance, the position and the lens. Imagen's guide lists macro at 60-105mm for objects and still life.

options.text: "A coffee bag. Don't shoot it from too far, don't use a bad lens, and don't make the framing boring."
options.explanation: This lists what to avoid. Describe the framing you want in positive words (chapter 1).

options.text: "A coffee bag on a counter, fisheye lens, aerial view from far away, with the whole café in the frame."
options.explanation: These are real camera words, but they push the bag far away. The brief needs the beans in close detail.

questions.prompt: What is the main problem with "make one square and crop it four ways"?

options.text: Nothing. Cropping is always fine, because the model draws extra room around the subject.
options.explanation: A crop only removes pixels. Cutting a square to 16:9 or 4:1 loses the top and bottom of the picture.

options.text: Square images cost more than any other size, so the plan wastes money on every placement.
options.explanation: The docs in this chapter don't say that. The problem is what a crop removes.

options.text: Cropping a square to 16:9 or 4:1 cuts off the top and bottom, so pick each ratio when you generate.
options.explanation: Right. Choose the ratio for the real use before you generate. Imagen's guide even gives a use for each ratio.

options.text: Square images are not allowed on OpenAI's models, so the first step of the plan will fail.
options.explanation: 1024x1024 (square) is one of OpenAI's common sizes.

questions.prompt: How do you make the 4:1 email banner?

options.text: Ask OpenAI for a custom size of 3840x960, which is exactly 4:1 and stays under the edge limit.
options.explanation: The edge is fine, but 4:1 breaks OpenAI's rule that the long edge is no more than 3 times the short edge.

options.text: Ask OpenAI for 4096x1024, which is a larger 4:1 size and gives you more detail for the banner.
options.explanation: This breaks two rules: 4096 is over the 3,840-pixel edge limit, and 4:1 is over the 3:1 ratio limit.

options.text: Write "very wide banner" in the prompt and keep the size at 1024x1024 so the model makes it wide.
options.explanation: The output shape comes from the size setting. A square size gives a square image.

options.text: Use a model whose list has 4:1, like Nano Banana 2.1, or make 3:1 on OpenAI and extend it yourself.
options.explanation: Right. Gemini's Nano Banana 2.1 lists 4:1. OpenAI caps the ratio at 3:1, so you generate within it and finish the width in your design tool.

questions.prompt: For the header you asked for the bag in the left third. It came back in the centre. What now?

options.text: Expect this: OpenAI lists composition control as a limit. Move or composite the bag in your design tool.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says the model may have difficulty placing elements precisely in layout-sensitive compositions. Its prompting guide suggests compositing when a part must be exact.

options.text: Add the word "exactly" five times to the prompt, and keep regenerating until the bag moves left.
options.explanation: Repeating a word does not fix a known limit. You may spend many runs and still miss.

options.text: Change the lens from macro to 50mm, because the lens setting is what decides where objects sit.
options.explanation: A lens word changes the look, not the position in the layout. OpenAI calls camera specs cues for appearance.

options.text: Report a bug to the vendor. The API must place every element exactly where you ask it to.
options.explanation: The docs list this as a known limitation, not a promise the API breaks.
